clue.text: Unusual tenants we met in various books

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of the following words are put into a new, unusual order

explanation.surface: Some odd lodgers you came across in assorted volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Testament is the collection of Christian scriptures, many separate writings bound together.

clue.text: Feeding arrangement began so differently

indicators.note: differently tells us to arrange the letters of the two preceding words in another way

explanation.surface: Something to do with feeding that started in another fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's food is hung in a bag over its head, a simple arrangement for eating on the move.

clue.text: Ill quit position in restaurant to work in garden

indicators.note: quit says the speaker, I, leaves the job title, so that letter goes

parts.note: a waiter is a job serving tables in a restaurant
Ill is printed for I'll, I will, giving the letter I as the one who quits

explanation.surface: Someone leaving a restaurant job to take up gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Ill' without its apostrophe; it is I'll, the I who leaves WAITER.
explanation.definitionFit: Watering plants is everyday garden work, so the verb fits the infinitive phrase.

clue.text: In previous venue, who in France is so refined?

indicators.note: In at the front says the French word sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: ex means former or previous, as in ex-wife
a site is a venue or location
qui is the French word for who

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Frenchman at an old haunt is particularly genteel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exquisite is extremely delicate and fine, so very refined.

clue.text: Gin in mouth

definitions.meaning: a gin is a snare for catching animals
slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your ...'

explanation.definitionFit: Both a snare for game and a slang word for the mouth share this one short word.

clue.text: Holding people up, girl wants a reminder

indicators.note: holding says the girl's name wraps round the other piece
wants in the sense of lacks, so the girl's name loses an A

parts.note: Monica is a girl's name

indicators.note: up in a down clue reads the word for people from the bottom upwards

parts.note: men is a word for people

explanation.surface: A girl holding up a crowd wants something to jog her memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants' means lacks, not desires; 'up' turns the word for people so it reads upwards inside the trimmed name.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory aid, such as a rhyme, helps one recall facts; it is a device that jogs the memory.

clue.text: Peer to see part of heel-bone dug up

indicators.note: dug up in a down clue means the run is read upwards, backwards
part of says the letters lie within the hyphenated word

explanation.surface: An archaeologist looking at a fragment of excavated heel bone.
explanation.walkthrough: The run ELBON in heEL-BONe, read upwards by 'dug up', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the aristocracy, such as a duke or earl.

clue.text: Talk? Just the opposite

definitions.meaning: the reverse or contrary of something

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to chat; as a noun, the reverse of a statement.

clue.text: Fill order with care

definitions.meaning: to load or fill, as a battery or a glass
custody, as in a child left in one's keeping

explanation.definitionFit: One word means to load up, to command, and custody or keeping.

clue.text: A request's processed for an instrument

indicators.note: processed means the letters are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's application is dealt with, all for the sake of some tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A set square is a triangular drawing instrument for right angles.

clue.text: The two right in the soup

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation goes inside the other word

parts.note: both means the two together

explanation.surface: A pair of people are in trouble, rightly in the soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' looks like the idiom for trouble, but 'soup' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin soup of meat or vegetables simmered in stock.

clue.text: Capital composer

definitions.meaning: Irving ..., the American songwriter of White Christmas

explanation.definitionFit: Germany's capital city shares its name with the songwriter Irving Berlin.

clue.text: Further short time needed to regain health after getting rid of cold

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a short time

indicators.note: after getting rid of says the letter for cold is removed

parts.note: to recover is to regain health
C is the abbreviation for cold, on taps

explanation.surface: A patient needs a bit more time to get well once the chill has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in addition, used to add a point to an argument.

clue.text: Spirit in mouth — nothing left?

parts.note: gob is British slang for mouth

indicators.note: left means read leftwards, from right to left, so backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A drinker asks whether any spirit remains in the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests drink, but it is a mischievous sprite.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblin is a mischievous supernatural creature in folklore, a kind of sprite.

clue.text: Stole minor record in aquatic event

parts.note: a boa is a long feathery stole worn round the neck
a trace is a faint mark or small record left behind

explanation.surface: Someone stole a small record during a water sports event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' reads as a verb but is the scarf. The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing race on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat race is a rowing contest on water.

clue.text: High as a kite with succession being assured, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak says the phrase is said out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: an heir born guarantees the succession to a title

explanation.surface: A dynasty celebrating the birth of an heir, everyone feeling elated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High as a kite' means drunk or elated, but here it means up in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flying aloft in the sky, like a kite, is up in the air.

clue.text: Inflated weapon — a whole string of them, almost

parts.note: a bomb is an explosive weapon

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a stick of bombs is a string dropped in one run

explanation.surface: A blown-up weapon, almost a whole stick of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombastic speech is pompous and puffed up, high-sounding but empty.

clue.text: Second alternative for "clamber?

indicators.note: alternative signals another arrangement of the word's letters

explanation.surface: A thesaurus query: is there a second word one could use instead of clamber?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer, a synonym for clamber.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble up a slope is to clamber, using hands and feet.

clue.text: Soldier led by sweetheart in dance

indicators.note: led by puts the sweetheart first, ahead of the soldier

parts.note: an old flame is a former sweetheart
NCO is a non-commissioned officer, a soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier being guided by his girlfriend during a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish gypsy dance with stamping and guitar.

clue.text: Following strict sectarians, feel very hungry

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, in page references
the Amish are a strict Christian sect in America

explanation.surface: After joining a strict sect, someone feels starved.
explanation.definitionFit: To famish is to be starving, from the same root as famine.

clue.text: Delay that's holding back heads of department, even prime minister

indicators.note: holding says the first piece wraps round the rest

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

indicators.note: back means the enclosed pieces are read in reverse
heads of picks the first letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A hold-up that keeps back department heads and even the PM.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is the Latin id est, and 'back' turns the two heads with the PM round to MPED before they are held.
explanation.definitionFit: To impede is to hinder or slow down, so to hold up.

clue.text: All but deserve to shoot through the sound barrier

indicators.note: all but means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to earn is to deserve
to plug someone is slang for shooting them

explanation.surface: Someone almost deserves to be shot for breaking the sound barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the sound barrier' suggests supersonic flight; here it is literally a barrier to sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A small stopper in the ear blocks out noise, a literal barrier against sound.

clue.text: Alarming activity on the sidelines

indicators.note: activity signals the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Something alarming happening off to the side of the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginal means at the edges, peripheral, not central.

clue.text: One kind of wood is just perfect

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
deal is fir or pine timber

explanation.surface: A single type of timber is exactly right.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect, exactly as one would wish.

clue.text: Defeat utterly in field event

definitions.meaning: to thrash or trounce an opponent
the athletics throwing event with a weighted ball on a wire

explanation.definitionFit: To trounce someone, and also the athletics throw with a ball on a wire.

clue.text: Legal expert in plain clothes

definitions.meaning: a Muslim scholar who gives rulings on Islamic law
civilian dress worn by someone normally in uniform

explanation.definitionFit: An Islamic jurist, and also civilian dress worn off duty by a soldier.

clue.text: Huge container holding last of hops.

indicators.note: holding says the container wraps round the letter

parts.note: a vat is a large container for liquids

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A huge brewing vessel with the last of the hops in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vast means immense or enormous.

clue.text: Plinth has century cut into underside

indicators.note: cut into says the abbreviation goes inside the other word

parts.note: the sole is the underside of a foot or shoe
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: A statue base has a hundred notches cut into its bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A socle is a low block or base supporting a column or statue.

clue.text: Lovely boyfriend? Wonderful girl's half ready to return

parts.note: a beau is a boyfriend

indicators.note: to return means these pieces are read backwards
half takes the first two of the four letters

parts.note: a lulu is something or someone outstanding
fit means ready or prepared

explanation.surface: Admiring a boyfriend and a wonderful girl who is half ready to go back.
explanation.walkthrough: A lulu is old slang for a remarkable person or thing; 'to return' turns the half and the word for ready round, giving TIFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something very attractive or pleasing.

clue.text: Athletic type keeping certain items for one who's intellectual

parts.note: a Blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge at sport
stocking means keeping goods in store

explanation.surface: A sportsman keeping certain goods turns out to be a bookish sort.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsman; a bluestocking is an intellectual woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluestocking is a scholarly, learned woman, a term once used mockingly.
